_setup: r-weekly-exec-update runs in the project 'exec-briefing' and follows the playbook 'p-weekly-exec-update'. The deployment creates that project with resource references (context packets {kind, ref, name, summary}) for: each designated weekly meeting (name = its exact Meet title; ref = its current folder, only a hint), the exec-summaries output folder, and the brand-guide doc. Deployment bindings are project resources — never memory, which consolidation prunes (BRAIN_CANON B-5). Without the project the mission says so and stops. Give the agent access to the notes by INVITING it to the meetings (with notes shared to invitees) — never by sharing the host's 'Google Meet' folder: since July 2026 Google answers a share of that root folder by starting a new one for every later meeting.

responsibilities.name: Weekly Executive Update
responsibilities.instruction: Produce this week's Weekly Executive Update to structure the 30-minute weekly executive sync. Read the designated meetings, the output folder and the brand-guide doc from this mission's PROJECT — they are its resource references (do not look them up in memory; do not use the calendar). For each designated meeting find its most recent notes BY THE MEETING'S NAME — its '- Transcript' doc, NOT the '- Recording' video — and SAVE the full text to a working file; gather every designated source you can, flag any source older than this week as stale, and if one is unavailable note it and proceed with the rest. Then synthesize a COMPLETE briefing — agenda-at-a-glance, State of the Week, per-area status with blockers, Decisions to Lock, and an owner/action/due table — where every section carries real content drawn from the transcripts (no empty or placeholder sections). Deliver it as ONE branded Google Doc titled 'Weekly Executive Update - <today's date>' in the output folder, CREATED fresh (an earlier doc with today's title goes to the trash first; ids copied verbatim; its sharing left exactly as the folder grants it) and report its link plus the section headings you read back.
responsibilities.success_criteria: This week's Weekly Executive Update exists as a branded Google Doc TITLED 'Weekly Executive Update - <today's date, YYYY-MM-DD>' (not the legacy 'Weekly Executive Brief', and using today's real date) in the exec-summaries output folder, and its link is reported — its sharing left exactly as the output folder grants it (never made public or link-shared). As evidence, the agent READ THE FINISHED DOCUMENT BACK and reported the exact section headings AND confirmed each has real, non-empty body content synthesized from the transcripts — an empty-section or placeholder document does NOT satisfy this. Required sections: agenda-at-a-glance, State of the Week, per-area status with blockers, Decisions to Lock, and an owner/action/due Action Items table. Sourced from each designated weekly meeting's most recent notes (a source older than this week is FLAGGED as stale in the briefing; a designated meeting with no readable notes is NOTED rather than blocking the work); no non-designated meeting is used; acronyms normalized (e.g. SOC 2); and exactly ONE doc for this week exists (an earlier same-day doc was moved to the trash, not duplicated).

context.purpose: Leadership runs a 30-minute weekly executive sync and needs one reliable, skimmable briefing, built the same way every week from that week's meeting notes.
process: READ THE PROJECT (do this first): this mission runs in its project, and the project's resource references — shown in its project context — are this deployment's weekly-exec specifics: the designated source meetings (each resource NAMED after its meeting, with its current folder as a hint), the exec-summaries OUTPUT folder, and the brand-guide doc. Copy every id VERBATIM from there. The playbook arrives as this mission's PLAYBOOK context — it is not a document to look up. If a required resource is missing from the project, say so and stop rather than guessing, searching memory, or using the calendar.

GATHER — full text of each source, saved to the workspace: for EACH designated meeting, find its MOST RECENT notes and save the FULL text to a file in your working directory (docs-cat <id> --out <meeting>.txt). Capturing full text to disk is REQUIRED so the document body is written from the full transcripts, not a lossy summary. Find each meeting's notes BY ITS NAME, not by one folder: drive-search --query "name contains '<the resource's meeting name>' and name contains 'Transcript'" --order-by "createdTime desc" — Google files meeting notes into 'Google Meet' folders it re-creates, and shares them file by file, so a folder id is only a hint; list the resource's folder only if the name search finds nothing. Read ONLY the doc whose name ends '- Transcript' (SKIP the '- Recording' video/mp4, which is not text); if no transcript is readable, that meeting's 'Notes by Gemini' doc is an acceptable source. Use ONLY your designated meetings; EXCLUDE every other meeting. If a meeting's most recent notes are older than this week, still use them and FLAG them as stale (with their date) so the room knows they are not new; if a meeting has no readable notes at all, NOTE that in one line and PROCEED with the sources you have — do NOT block, and do NOT retry a missing source more than once.

SYNTHESIZE from the SAVED files (never from a summary): read the saved files back and distill them into a content JSON in the docs-create-branded --content format — an array of section objects such as {"type":"heading","level":2,"text":"..."}, {"type":"paragraph","text":"..."}, {"type":"bullet_list","items":["..."]}, {"type":"table","headers":[...],"rows":[[...]]}. EVERY heading MUST be followed by paragraph/bullet/table sections carrying the ACTUAL substance from the transcripts — specific decisions, owners, risks, dates, numbers. NEVER emit a heading with no body, and never use placeholder text; an empty or placeholder section is a FAILURE. Include exactly these top-level sections in order: 'Agenda-at-a-Glance' (the segments + rough time boxes summing to ~30 min), 'State of the Week' (what shipped, biggest risk, focus, binding constraint), per-area status (group the areas that appear in the notes, blockers inline), 'Decisions to Lock', and an owner/action/due Action Items table (5-10 top items). Normalize acronyms (e.g. 'Sock 2' -> SOC 2). About three pages.

DELIVER in one step, from the JSON you built: FIRST list the OUTPUT folder — that listing is the ONLY truth about what exists there; never reuse a doc id carried over from recall or an earlier run (it may have been trashed). If the listing shows a doc titled 'Weekly Executive Update - <today's date>', move it to the trash (drive-delete --file <its id>) so exactly one doc remains. Then CREATE the briefing fresh with docs-create-branded --title "Weekly Executive Update - <TODAY's actual date, YYYY-MM-DD>" --content <your content json file> --brand-doc <brand-guide id from the project> --folder <output folder id from the project> — creating is the path that carries the whole structure. NEVER change the doc's sharing (no drive-share, no public or anyone-with-the-link access): it inherits the output folder's access, and its link already works for everyone who should read it. Use TODAY's real date in the title — never a meeting date or a future date; the title must read 'Weekly Executive Update - <date>' (not 'Brief'). Copy every id EXACTLY from the project's resources (verbatim).

VERIFY with evidence: read the finished doc back and report (a) the section headings AND, for each, that it has real non-empty body content — an empty-section doc does NOT count as done; (b) the source transcripts you used, with their dates (and any designated source you had to skip or flag as stale); (c) the doc's link, exactly as created (its sharing unchanged). That read-back is the proof.
